newsitem.title: USA: US money managers mostly unchanged on debt-survey.
newsitem.headline: US money managers mostly unchanged on debt-survey.

text.p: Money managers were a little cautious of the U.S. debt markets, but made virtually no changes to their portfolio structures over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Money managers remained close to flat and somewhat cautious on the market," the report said.

Most of the data was collected prior to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony Tuesday afternoon. And the rate of participation of respondents was lower than usual because of summer holidays, it said.
In the week ended July 22, the cash/assets ratio rose 8.16 percent from 7.92 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 6.02 percent from 6.15 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 100.54 percent from 100.06 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 99.35 percent from 99.13 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 4.92 from 4.70 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 4.53 from 4.48 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Thirteen percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 9 percent the week ending July 15.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
